subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser/per-channel lane routing, fold this into broader per-agent lane work, or use a different scheduler fairness policy such as foreground reserves?
rationale: The implementation primitives exist, but exposing lane routing changes public config, fairness guarantees, and resource-cap behavior across channels and upgrades.

options.title: Design lane routing policy
options.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design that covers browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

options.title: Fold into per-agent lanes
options.body: Treat this as a browser-specific use case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 and keep per-channel/browser routing out unless per-agent isolation proves insufficient.

options.title: Prefer priority fairness
options.body: Avoid new lane config for now and instead pursue foreground reserve or priority-aging work that keeps fast user turns responsive on the shared lane.

recommendation.title: Design lane routing policy
recommendation.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design that covers browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current local blame places the main-lane admission and queue primitives under this contributor, making them the best available routing owner from history.
